name: recruitment-baseline
title: Baseline: cue + response recruits

purpose.question:
When source cells secrete a diffusible cue and responder cells carry a
competent chemotactic response, do responders migrate up the gradient and
accumulate at the source?

report.title: Baseline: a secreted cue recruits competent responders
report.objective: Simulate the CPM recruitment world (source slab + six responders in the gradient zone), equilibrate the secreted field, and measure the recruitment index over 500 MC sweeps across 5 seeds.
report.conclusion: Cue + competent response recruits: the final recruitment index is 0.767 ± 0.170 across 5 seeds, versus 0.000 for both negative conditions (Cohen's d = 6.38).
report.main_insight: Recruitment is an emergent collective outcome of local chemotactic copy-attempt biases, not an engineered per-cell rule.
report.caveat: The chemotaxis lambda is a PHENOMENOLOGICAL response strength, not a receptor-level model — a deliberate semantic gap the receptor arm closes.

study_card.goal: Show that a secreted cue plus a competent chemotactic response recruits responders to the source.
study_card.mechanism: Type-1 source cells secrete field C; type-2 responders chemotax up the gradient (lambda=14).
study_card.why_before_next: The anchoring positive condition — the ground truth the receptor realization must reproduce.
study_card.expected_result: Recruitment index rises from 0 to a plateau ~0.67–0.83; mean approach > 0.4.
study_card.main_expert_question: Is a phenomenological chemotaxis lambda an acceptable stand-in for receptor-gated response at this level?

question:
When source cells secrete a diffusible cue and responder cells carry a
competent chemotactic response, do the responders directionally migrate up the
gradient and accumulate at the source?
hypothesis:
With the cue secreted (rate 10) and the response intact (lambda 14), responder
centres of mass move toward the source region and the recruitment index rises
well above zero.
objective:
Simulate the CPM recruitment world (source slab + six responders in the gradient
zone), equilibrate the secreted field, and measure the recruitment index —
fraction of responders within 15 px of the source — over 500 MC sweeps.
description:
The anchoring positive condition of the chemotactic-recruitment slice. Type-1
source cells secrete field C (d=0.22, decay=0.001); type-2 responders start ~33 px
away and chemotax up the gradient with strength lambda=14. This is the native
viva-cpm realization of the biological claim "a secreted cue recruits responder
cells", and the ground-truth study the Biological Claim Layer compiler must
reproduce.
claim:
Responders climb the secreted gradient and are recruited to the source: the
recruitment index rises from 0 to a plateau of ~0.67-0.83 (mean approach 0.61).
expected_behavior: Responder mean distance to the source falls substantially over the run.
Recruitment index rises above 0.5 (a majority of responders reach the source region).

0.4. Measured from the run: recruitment index 0.000 -> 0.667 (peak 0.833),
mean approach 0.608.

findings.statement:
Cue + competent response recruits: across 5 independent seeds the final
recruitment index is 0.767 +/- 0.170, versus 0.000 +/- 0.000 for both negative
conditions (Cohen's d = 6.38). Recruitment is an emergent collective outcome of
local chemotactic copy-attempt biases, not an engineered per-cell rule.

controls.name: No cue yields no recruitment (recruitment-adversarial)
controls.test: Responders are recruited to the source
controls.description: Competent responders with no cue are not recruited (negative control).

controls.name: Response blocked (recruitment-inhibited)
controls.test: Responders are recruited to the source
controls.description: With the cue present but lambda=0, recruitment is abolished.

alternative_hypotheses.claim: Responders accumulate by random diffusion, not by climbing the cue gradient.
alternative_hypotheses.discriminated_by: Responders are recruited to the source
alternative_hypotheses.note: Excluded by the inhibited arm — lambda=0 abolishes recruitment despite the cue present.

alternative_hypotheses.claim: The recruitment signal is a metric artifact (spurious proximity counting).
alternative_hypotheses.discriminated_by: Responders are recruited to the source
alternative_hypotheses.note: Excluded by the adversarial arm — no cue leaves the recruitment index at 0.

conclusion:
The native CPM realization reproduces cue-driven recruitment. Fidelity note:
the CPM chemotaxis lambda is a PHENOMENOLOGICAL response strength (a bias on the
copy-attempt energy), not a receptor-level model — a deliberate semantic-gap the
realization records rather than hides.

regression_compatibility.basis: Reproduces the expected CPM recruitment behaviour with the declared energies and ICs.

biological_validation.basis: Recruitment index 0.767 ± 0.170 vs 0.000 for both negative controls (Cohen's d = 6.38, 5 seeds).

explanatory_gain.basis: Recruitment emerges from local copy-attempt biases rather than an imposed per-cell rule.

biological_summary:
Source cells secrete a diffusible chemokine that forms a spatial gradient from
the source slab into the responder zone. Responder cells bias their Cellular
Potts copy attempts up the local gradient (chemotaxis strength lambda), so over
~500 Monte-Carlo sweeps their centres of mass drift toward the source and a
majority end up within the recruitment radius. Removing either ingredient — the
cue (adversarial arm) or the response (inhibited arm) — abolishes recruitment,
establishing that both are necessary. This is the phenomenological realization
of the biological claim "a secreted cue recruits responder cells".

literature_anchors.expectation: Responder cells climb a secreted chemokine gradient toward the source.
literature_anchors.status_in_workspace: Verified — observed value matches (0.767 vs 0 controls)

key_assumptions: Field diffusion capped at d<=0.25 for numerical stability; gradient equilibrated with 600 advance_fields sweeps before cell stepping.
Recruitment radius = 15 px (source at x~10; responders start at x~43).

model_change.notes:
Realizes the recruitment claim with one parameterized CPMProcess. Type-1
source cells secrete field C (d=0.22, decay=0.001) at cue_rate; type-2
responders chemotax up the local gradient with strength chemo_lambda — a
phenomenological copy-attempt bias on the existing CPM engine. No new
processes, state variables, or listeners were added.

design_pivot_required.question: Represent the chemotactic response as a phenomenological lambda or a receptor-level model?
design_pivot_required.notes:
Resolved by building BOTH rungs: this study anchors the claim with a
phenomenological lambda; the receptor arm refines it to a Kd-calibrated
Hill occupancy. The semantic gap is recorded, not hidden.
